elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to an Affiliate without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The first sentence expressly permits this, but the retained sentence declaring “Any attempt to assign this Agreement ... without such consent” void is unqualified and contradicts the consent-free Affiliate carve-out.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor in a merger without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Although expressly permitted in the first sentence, the retained unqualified voidness sentence can render an assignment made without consent void.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor in an acquisition without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Although expressly permitted in the first sentence, the retained unqualified voidness sentence can render an assignment made without consent void.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor in a sale of substantially all of its assets without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Although expressly permitted in the first sentence, the retained unqualified voidness sentence can render an assignment made without consent void.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign the Agreement without Customer's prior written consent.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Licensor may not assign the Agreement without Licensee's prior written consent.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Vendor assignment.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that Licensee's consent “will not be unreasonably withheld.”

elements.element: Vendor may never assign the Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause independently provides that Licensor “may not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Licensee.”

elements.element: Customer's Change of Control gives Vendor no right to terminate the Agreement or Customer's rights or licenses.
elements.evidence: The automatic-termination language is removed and replaced with an express statement that a Change of Control gives Licensor no right to terminate the Agreement or any Licensee rights or licenses.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The clause provides a consent-free right for specified M&A successors, but the retained unqualified voidness sentence contradicts the effectiveness of an assignment made without consent.

elements.element: Customer must provide written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: No operative written-notice obligation applies to Licensee's successor assignments.

elements.element: Vendor may assign the Agreement to a successor without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: All Licensor assignments require Licensee's prior written consent; there is no successor exception.

elements.element: Vendor must provide written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: No notice-based successor-assignment mechanism or written-notice obligation is provided for Licensor.

elements.element: Customer assignments other than assignments to successors require Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Affiliate assignments are expressly permitted without consent even though an Affiliate need not be a successor; the retained voidness sentence also makes the consent regime internally inconsistent.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to Customer assignments other than assignments to successors.
elements.evidence: Licensee's other assignments require Licensor consent, but there is no requirement that Licensor not unreasonably withhold that consent.

elements.element: Vendor assignments other than assignments to successors require Customer consent.
elements.evidence: The clause requires Licensee's prior written consent for every Licensor assignment, including non-successor assignments.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to Vendor assignments other than assignments to successors.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that Licensee's consent to a Licensor assignment will not be unreasonably withheld, although competitor assignments are independently prohibited.

result.reason: The redline adds the requested preferred protections, but the retained sentence making any Licensee assignment made “without such consent” void directly conflicts with the new consent-free Affiliate and M&A carve-outs. It should instead apply only to assignments requiring consent under the section. Because that contradiction prevents a complete preferred position, and the fallback's mutual notice-based successor regime is also absent, neither level is fully satisfied.
